item.description: A day after Craig Whyte's death at the Osborn Correctional Institution, his mom and siblings have engaged local attorney Ken Krayeske to help find out what happened -- as they mourn the loss of a devoted sibling, roofer, lover of reggae music, and proud Jamaican immigrant known to friends and family as "Sizzla."

item.title: 1 Dead After Blvd. Crash - New Haven Independent
item.description: One person died and two were injured following a two-car crash on Ella T. Grasso Boulevard Tuesday morning. According to a city police spokesperson and a state police spokesperson, one of the involved vehicles had sped away from a state trooper's attempt to pull the car over soon before the fatal collision occurred.

item.title: Mayor's Budget Would Cut Food Aid - New Haven Independent
item.description: Meal distributions for kids on school break. Grants for small food pantries in need of supplies. A pair of outreach workers helping residents navigate increasingly arduous SNAP requirements. Those food-aid initiatives are slated to lose city funding in the coming fiscal year — unless the alders amend the mayor's proposed budget.

item.title: Supt. Proposes $252M Schools Budget - New Haven Independent
item.description: New Haven Public Schools (NHPS) Supt. Madeline Negrón presented a $252 million budget proposal to the Board of Education Monday -- explaining that the 18.5 percent increase is needed to help the district continue to “yield significant gains” around reducing chronic absenteeism and increasing graduation rates.

item.title: British MPs Impressed By Bioswales - New Haven Independent
item.description: Six British lawmakers spent Tuesday in New Haven visiting bioswales, Yale's quantum technology lab, and an art gallery -- as part of the U.K.'s broader effort to deepen ties with individual states amid uncertainty in Washington, D.C.

item.title: Elicker Picks Zannelli To Be Next Police Chief - New Haven Independent
item.description: Mayor Justin Elicker plans to nominate Acting Police Chief David Zannelli to serve as the city's next permanent chief, more than two-and-a-half months after Zannelli's predecessor, Karl Jacobson, abruptly retired -- and was later arrested -- for allegedly stealing public funds.
